# Overland

> Overland is a free, self-guided guide to running London's whole transport network above ground — Tube, Overground, DLR and Elizabeth lines, National Rail commuter lines, trams, bus routes, the Superloop, the London LOOP and Capital Ring, plus disused railways, rivers, canals and parks — one line at a time, at your own pace, whenever you like. This file is a guide for AI agents, LLM tools and crawlers.

Site: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/

The site is a static single-page app on GitHub Pages. There is no server API — the JSON/GeoJSON/GPX files below are the API. Everything is served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, no auth, no key, no rate limit beyond GitHub Pages itself. Coordinates are WGS84; `[lat, lon]` pair order unless a format (GeoJSON, GPX) dictates otherwise. Distances are kilometres.

## The basics

- Self-guided: there is no club, no fixture list and no signup. Pick a line, take its distance and route, and run, walk or ride it end to end whenever suits you. Free, all paces.
- The site still publishes a suggested calendar — mostly the first Sunday of each month, plus dated multi-day and disused-line adventures. It is a prompt, not a meetup; distances and escape points are in the Schedule section.
- Suggested runs as data: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/schedule.json — `{ club, site, generated, rule, runs: [{ date, days, status: confirmed|suggested, kind, name, line, leg, start, distance, location, routeLink, notes, exits }] }`. Regenerated by the pre-commit hook whenever a commit touches script.js, from the same source the site renders.

## Network data

- Tube network: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/tube-network.json
  18 TfL lines (Underground, Overground lines, Elizabeth, DLR, Tram) as `{ <lineId>: { name, colour, stations: { <naptanId>: { n, lat, lon } }, branches: [[naptanId, …]], route: [naptanId, …] } }`. `route` is the displayed main line, reading London-outward.
- National Rail network: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/nr-network.json
  10 commuter operators (SWR, Southern, Southeastern, Thameslink, GWR, Chiltern, c2c, Great Northern, Greater Anglia, Heathrow Express) in the same shape, clipped to the commuter belt (lat 50.75–51.95, lon −1.15–0.75). Main routes are anchored at each operator's London terminus.
- Line geometry: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/tube-lines.geojson and https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/nr-lines.geojson
  GeoJSON MultiLineString per line, properties `{ line, name, colour }`.

## Runnable route data

- Main-line pavement routes: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/routes/<lineId>.gpx (e.g. `routes/district.gpx`, `routes/south-western-railway.gpx`)
  GPX of the on-foot route tracing each line's main route, with station waypoints.
- NR branch pavements: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/nr-branch-routes.json
  `{ <lineId>: [ [[lat, lon], …], … ] }` — street-level polylines for every non-main branch.
- Named running routes: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/routes.geojson
  Parks, rivers, canals and disused railways (Parkland Walk, Crystal Palace High Level, Longmoor Military Railway, …) as GeoJSON features.
- Variant pavements: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/variant-routes.json

## Extras

- Post-run pubs near each route: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/route-pubs.json
- Hidden gems / points of interest: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/secrets.json — `[{ n, k, lat, lon, d }]` (name, kind, coords, description).
- London borough boundaries: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/boroughs.json
- Station toilets: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/station-toilets.json
- Drinking fountains: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/facilities-water.json
- Bus route ids: https://psurma.github.io/Overland/data/bus-routes.json — flat list of London bus route numbers; stops and geometry are fetched live from the TfL Unified API (api.tfl.gov.uk) by the site.

## Notes for agents

- Attribution: "Overland — a guide to running London above ground, https://psurma.github.io/Overland/". Network data derives from the TfL Unified API; route pavements from OSM via BRouter.
- Data files are versioned with the site and change when the site deploys; they are safe to cache briefly.
- The page itself renders everything client-side; prefer the data files above over scraping the DOM.
